reviews.author: harikrishnag
reviews.review_text:
Well, I lived in this apartments for 10  years and finally I vacated in the month of August. The lease system is not to update and it has lot of flaws. I was supposed to renew my lease in May 2011. They never sent the lease renewal notice and as I was staying there years and years, I didn't check either. In February 2012, they alerted me about the missing renewal and I said I will renew it. They asked me to renew the lease as per the original dates i.e from May 2011 to May 31, 2012. They use the 3rd party web site to sign the lease digitally. The sales representative sent the lease with the dates from Feb 1, 2012 to Jan 31, 2013, thinking that the lease starts from that month. I went back and asked about the dates. They corrected and generated new lease documents. We both (me and my wife) signed the lease. From May 2012, I was going on month-to-month basis and in July 1st week, I gave the 1 month notice to vacate in August. After vacating the apartment, I got the bill for breaking the lease. I went there and talked to account manager and she told that I signed a lease from Feb 2012, Jan 2013 - which I didn't sign. She showed me the lease agreement where it shows that we both signed the lease on Jun 6th. The lease was generated in February and asked them to correct it, but they corrected and generated the new one, but forgot to delete the wrong one. I think that existed in the system, and on June 6th some one checked and would have thought this was supposed to sign in the month of Feb 2012 itself and they would have marked it as signed. But the account manager didn't agree with my theory and asked me to check with the 3rd party software/site if I have questions on who actually signed the lease. I tried my level best to convince her. In that process I repeated some of the questions 2 to 3 times, because I wanted to clarify my doubts. She got irritated with my questions and told that there are lot of customers waiting and I need to leave and pay the balance. I asked for the copies of the lease and went home and started checking the lease documents. It clearly shows, on June 6th, 2012, the lease was signed by 3 different people (me, my wife and apartment sales representative) from the same ip address with the seconds difference. My wife traveled abroad during that time frame and I have the proofs of her itinerary and stamps on the passport about her departure and arrival. So it is impossible for 3 of us to sign the lease from same ip address. So it is clear that we didn't sign the lease. I went back and showed the same ip address on the lease and asked to remove the lease breaking charges and send me the updated bill. I tried to talk to the manager on that day, but she was busy and mentioned that she cannot give the appointment for next 4 days. A week after, they sent to the collection agency. I tried to talk to them again to remove the lease breaking charges, but they said it's with collection agency and cannot talk about it at all. I asked if I pay to collection agency and once you receive the money, can you refund the lease breaking charges, but the account manager told that they cannot do anything about this. They said I don't have an option to talk about it. 

In short, unacceptable responses from the management even though there is a clear evidence that I didn't sign the lease. I am not sure, this is even considered as forgery. Clearly we didn't sign the lease and they are not even open to talk about it and correct it.

I am not recommending this apartment to any one at all and stay away from this.

reviews.review_text:
Ok, so here are the straight facts on this place.

Solara is a BEAUTIFUL remodeled community with meandering walkways and attractive landscaping. Situated in a sought-after location by the airport, Mill Ave District, and major highways- Solara features 3 POOLS. One of which is heated over the winter (does Tempe even have winter?). The office staff is friendly and effective. I consider myself a discerning tenant, especially coming from a real estate background. I physically visited 13 other apartment communities in the 3 days prior to choosing Solara.

For starters, the leasing agent I worked with was the best of all the communities I'd visited- not by a little, by FAR. He was personable, competent, knowledgeable, and not at all salesy. I found a great unit next to the pool, at the best VALUE for my money. I signed a lease same day- and this staff member stayed late on New Year's Eve just so I could get keys that night.

Since move in, I've been very happy with with my experience here. The units are updated, and were UPDATED SMART and effectively. If you're in construction, you'd know what I mean. They did a great job modernizing the units without any major construction, probably helping keep rents so affordable. Mine has nearly all new appliances, a GAS RANGE, brand new carpets, and fresh paint. Behind the walls and ceiling is cement. I haven't heard a sound from my neighbors since I've lived here (the girl above me even has yappy dogs!). The window glass is likely single pane- but it's an EXTREMELY QUIET complex. Unless you're unlucky enough to have someone engaged in a loud conversation about 2 feet from your window, you really have nothing to worry about. The times that I've placed maintenance requests were only for minor items, to keep the place looking GREAT (I can be a little OCD..). It's worth noting that recently, a blonde staff member in the office took my very minor work order and made me feel TOTALLY APPRECIATED... like it was the most important issue of the day! She followed up so well, I would get unexpected calls with little updates and just to let me know she cared and was working on it. I felt spoiled.

Maintenance has always been fast, responsive, and friendly. One I met from Flagstaff was really a good guy. If there was a chance they were busy and wouldn't be able to make it over that day to take care of an issue, the office staff would always let me know ahead of time. And sometimes maintenance would even make it over anyway.

The one concern that I have with Solara is safety and theft. Once of my neighbors had his apartment broken into and robbed twice and a person above me had her window pried opened but nothing stolen. There are a couple of areas nearby that have had other problems recently. I don't think Solara is especially unique in that and I'm sure other communities throughout Tempe contend with the same issues. However, Solara could do a better job keeping the gates CLOSED, especially at night. They fixed 2 of the front vehicle gates but there are others which remain open, including the gates by the back mailboxes. I think that if Solara made it a priority to take care of this issue it would be the biggest step they could take to creating a truly incredible living environment. I'd give Solara 5 stars overall.

reviews.review_text:
It wouldn't be fair of me to not leave a review for these apartments. I have lived here for a year now and it has been one of the worst rental experiences of my life. 

One year ago I signed a lease for a ground-floor 2 bedroom 2 bathroom apartment. The night we moved in our sink overflowed with our neighbors runoff from there laundry machine. After putting in multiple complaints with the office, they finally sent a plumber to clean out our sink. All of the maintenance staff for Solara seemed amazed at the fact this was happening so I figured this should be the end of it. Within the week it occurred again. The second maintenance worker figured the problem would be resolved by "running water through the sink to dislodge the clog created by the plumber." Again, I had hopes this would help, but highly doubted the logic of the employee. Since then, this has occurred numerous times and I have been told by management that this is, "something that I will just have to live with." When I confronted the head of maintenance about this, he informed me that this is a problem with one out of every four apartments due to the style of the plumbing. This was definitely not something I was informed of prior to signing my lease.

The next issue began two months into the lease and has continued the entirety of my term. We received our bill in the mail and were shocked to see that a mysterious $35 charge was added. Now, I understand that isn't much, but being a college student on a budget, every little bit counts. I went to the management to figure out where this charge came from and was informed that this was an error in their billing system. They assured me this would not occur again. Sadly, this has occurred 10 times now and IS NOT BECAUSE OF LATE RENT. Each month, I had to walk to the office where they assured me that a "billing error" was the reason for the charge. I was even reassured by the district manager of Holland Residential that this issue would be resolved. 

The staff at Solara is constantly changing. Don't expect the agent that handles the signing of your lease to be employed longer than a month or two. Not only are they constantly hiring new staff members, who never take the time to remember names or faces, but they are some of the rudest and most judgmental people I have met. One employee in particular, who I will name "L" is the worst. Not once have I been greeted by her or seen her greet a resident in the many times I have been to the office the past four months of her employment. She talks down to you as if you don't understand English and when questioned about a policy, treats it as an attack. 

Near the end of my lease, I was looking for new locations and decided to see what rate I would get on a single bedroom/bathroom  at Solara and if continuing my lease would result in any discounts on the rent. When I arrived at the office I was again handled by "L" who informed me that before I could see what rates and rooms were available I would need to sign paperwork guaranteeing my stay for another year, as well as, pay an $80 fee. This was also required before I could even see what the model unit looked like. When my girlfriend, who was with me, asked what the rates would be for a non-continuing resident,  L  again informed us that the paperwork would need to be signed before any tours or quotes could be given.

Finally, they make many promises that they will not keep. Upon signing my lease, I was assured that the fixed utility rate would not increase as the lease contracts all prices including utility rate. However, December 15th, 2011, I received a notice stating that as of January 1st, 2012, utilities would increase, per unit, by $17.80. I was also assured during the lease signing that when the lease was up, a 30 day notice of moving out would be required by the office. It is now 42 days until my lease expires and I was informed by "L" that the notice requires 60 days and that I would have to wait 60 days from submitting the paperwork to leave, which would result in my rent increasing by nearly $300 to the month-by-month rate for the remainder of my lease. 

I understand that I m only one person and that everyone s experiences at Solara may differ, but I find it very hard to believe that all of this would occur during one lease. Please take this to heart when considering Solara. I don't want anyone to go through the annoyances I had to endure.

The grounds are decent and the apartments are roomy. But most of them are old and have cheap parts. Some of the office staff can be dismissive and downright rude at times (Harlie and Todd are the only ones I feel like actually care about their jobs). Maintenance is awful. Be prepared to fight for any areas you need fixed and stay on them, otherwise it won't get done. Renewals have been pretty high. I pay almost $200 more a month now than when I moved in three years ago. There are flat rate utilities, but those can and have increased mid rent cycle multiple times. And there are frequent issues with plumbing and AC, so on average at least once a week, one of them is not working and needs to be turned off.

Biggest issue is the apartments are HOT in the winter. They control the AC and will not turn it on until it's "warm" out. The apartments are poorly ventilated with large glass walls that will cook your rooms with no way to cool them off (literally I have two square foot windows in my bedroom and living room that are in the corner of the room with no way to help airflow).

I will say the grounds are clean and the remodel has helped the exterior look nicer and I have never had a bug problem besides a few ants, but that's about all it has going for it.

Oh and if you don't like college neighbors, stay away. Shame on me for not thinking that college kids would be loud at all hours of the day and night, but I have had a string of noisy neighbors. I don't even use my living room any more because I can't hear my TV over the noise most nights.

Oh and there are safety issues too. The "security gates" have no code or locks, so they are open most of the time. Even when they're closed, you can just pull up close and they will open automatically. I've come home more than once to cops. And there are on again off again drug problems. And a group of transients who will hang out in the complex during the day. I don't feel safe a lot of the time and am very grateful I have a dog.

Bottom line, I don't think they care about making this complex actually BE better, they're just making it look better.

With every bad experience, I've tried giving these people the benefit of the doubt by assuming it was just a one-time thing and that their management would get better should there be a "next time." Hope you're prepared to read this because tonight was the last straw for me. 

With the countless issues I've had here, I'm going to outline a few because they are my favorite examples of why nobody should live here. 

Last night my sink randomly flooded my entire kitchen. I came home from work to my cabinets open and a plunger sitting next to my kitchen sink, but the problem had still not been resolved. Thinking that maybe it could just be clogged or something that was our fault, I went to the store and bought 2 large bottles of Drain-o, came home and filled both sides of the sink. That still not resolving the problem, I called and asked if the maintenance guy could come back and finish fixing it, which they said was no problem and that he "should be there shortly." Three hours passes and he literally doesn't even show up. It's now 9:30 at night and every time the upstairs neighbor uses their water, my sink starts overflowing with disgusting liquid. I called the apartment hotline literally ten times and every time it prompts you to press a number all you hear is "invalid option" with an immediate hang up following it. The emergency maintenance line doesn't work, the message option doesn't work so I can't even leave management a message telling them that because their maintenance guy didn't show up, I now have a lake in my kitchen. I am quite literally wearing boots in my kitchen (because any other shoe would not suffice to keep my feet from getting disgusting) and filling buckets with water because there is so much of it and nobody in this apartment complex can help because the office just so happens to be closed and that is THE ONLY way you can get ahold of anyone (depending on if they actually answer the phone.)

Here's another fun example:

About a month ago there was a death in my immediate family and my sister had to fly across the country to try to help out with the funeral. She would only be gone for a maximum of 3 days, so i didn't see the issue with watching her animal while she was away in an obviously extreme case. A day later I get an eviction notice on my door saying that if I don't pay a fine of $175 and remove the animal immediately, I will be removed from the property. When calling management, (which, by the way is a Godsend if they ever actually answer.) I was put on the phone with 3 people who are obviously incapable of human emotion. Erin tried to help me work something out but they still didn't drop the fee, which I thought was pretty ridiculous considering it's a death in the family and not a permanent situation. Keep in mind that I'm the only other family member in Arizona, a full time student and have a full time job. I've never been late on rent and never had any issues on my end with Solara. 

Or here's a nice one if you enjoy cops! They are here every. single. night. Normally I would think "Oh, I'm a young girl, I like having a police officer around in case something bad ever happens." Not in this apartment complex. When you don't have sketchy people following you home when you're working out at night then banging on your door at 3 in the morning and leaving creepy notes (yes, this literally happened), you have cops raiding your next-door neighbor, complete with full body armor and riot shields! It makes you feel REALLY at home. Because who wouldn't want to come home from a long day at work to that, right? THEN when you call the office to ask what the hell is going on, they say "oh, someone couldn't get into their apartment and it was a safety issue." I'm just going to stop right there, because obviously you guys get the point. 

I can't even go into every time they've managed to piss me off because this would be way longer than it is now. I'm done. I know it seems nice because it's affordable and you can take the orbit to campus, but please just do yourself a favor and spare the hair-tearing out by not moving in. It's not in a nice neighborhood. You will literally be so upset with your decision, and this is coming from someone who literally waited a year before writing a bad review because I wanted to see the good in this complex. I'm sorry if I put a damper in your apartment-seeking process but I wish I had taken the reviews before me more seriously.

reviews.review_text:
I have lived at Solara at Mill Avenue since 2009.  Unfortunately, it has not been the best experience.  The worst part of my experience has been the management and office staff.  They are very unprofessional and offer incorrect information.  Some of the issues I had were every year, regardless of how long I had stayed with them, my rent would go up by $100-200 to where I finally couldn't afford staying there any longer.  Utilities were included, which was a plus, however, you could not control the air.  I had put on my lease I had cats, and was given the wrong amount for the pet deposit and had to pay additional fees because I was given the wrong information.  

I also had an issue with my apartment facing the sun when it was hottest in the day, and the entire wall was a window.  The windows were great, until summer.  I placed thermal curtains in the window and after two years of having them in the windows was told to "take them down" to have a uniform community.  I asked management how I can hang my curtains, without a way to keep the thermal curtains in the windows?  I had to have the tension rods in the window, in front of the blinds, as there was no wall to hang the curtains.  They brought me to the "show" apartment and showed how they hung the curtains, which was not the same window in my apartment.  I brought the office staff to my apartment and showed them my issue, and they stated "I don't know, figure it out".  

After this, I continued to get 10 Day Notices of intent to terminate my lease due to stupid issues that they never had called me about.  They just placed a notice on my door without calling me.  When I attempted to call about the issues, they would never call back after I left a message.  I received notices for having my cats, when they were on my lease, and not having the 300,000.00 in liability insurance requested.  I had insurance, just not the $300,000 they requested.  When I did have it, they gave me a notice for when it got transferred to my new home owners policy, even though I was moving out.  I had received 3-4 10 day notices in two months.

When I was moving out, they had confused my date of move out.  I gave my notice in January of 2014 and when I paid my rent in February, they called asking "I thought you were moving out?".  They require a 60 day notice, which is what I gave.  Maintenance came by my apartment 3-4 times because they couldn't remember when I was moving out.  When I went to obtain the information to break my lease, they had my file on Wednesday and had given me the amount.  I went back Thursday to pay the amount to break my lease, they had lost my file and continued to ask if I had given 60 day notice. 

They are completely unprofessional and unkind, and do not appear to know what they are doing.  On top of that, I had been notifying them since the beginning that I moved in that there was green or gray mold or mildew growing on the vents in my apartment.  They never came to fix the said issues, and it got worse over the years.  My grandparents say its due to the cooler system they use, but I am almost positive they will charge me for this even though I have told them for the past four years it has been on my grates since I moved in.

This apartment complex always states "Contact us, and we will attempt to help", but no one ever does.  I call and leave messages and get no calls back.  I get 10 day notices to terminate my lease without a single phone call from anyone in management or the office. I received no help for issues in my apartment and whenever I went up to the office was always waiting on the office staff to speak to me (They were either on their cell phones texting, or talking to each other).
